sections.h2: What is the Green, Ohio housing market like?
sections.html:
Green lies in the southeast corner of Summit County, between Akron and Canton, and covers an unusually wide area for a suburb at 32.03 square miles of land plus 1.5 square miles of water. That makes for a spread-out market of subdivisions, lakeside lots and former farm parcels rather than a compact grid.

Green Township was created in 1809 as part of Stark County and joined Summit County when that county formed in 1840. Hamlets such as Greensburg dotted the township, farms gave way to developers after 1950, and voters approved merging the village with the rest of the township in 1991. Green was a collection of farms, hamlets and coal-bearing land by 1900, and the local economy then shifted toward business and manufacturing. The city's motto, "A township from the past, a city of the future," reflects that history.

Green uses ZIP codes 44232, 44312, 44319, 44685 and 44216, and some of those addresses are shared with neighboring places. Ask the Summit County Fiscal Office to confirm that your parcel is inside the city limits before you rely on city rules.

sections.h2: How much does a typical Green home cost, by Census data?
sections.html:
Green skews toward owners: 75.1 percent of households own, the middle owned home is valued at $280,200, and the middle household earns $95,047.

The 2020 count was 27,475, with a median age of 43.1 and 5.3 percent of 11,825 housing units sitting vacant. QuickFacts adds that 89.7 percent of residents were in the same house a year before, 42.4 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, 93.9 percent of households have broadband, and the average commute is 23.7 minutes. Retail sales in 2022 came to $1,355,338,000, about $49,708 per resident.

The business rows give 2022 receipts of $492,696,000 for transportation and warehousing, $265,218,000 for health care and social assistance, and $100,627,000 for lodging and food service. The city counts 1,093 veterans, and 3.0 percent of residents were born abroad.

sections.h2: How fast has Green grown, and who lives in its homes?
sections.html:
Green added residents at every count: 22,817 in 2000, 25,699 in 2010 and 27,475 in 2020, with the 2025 estimate at 27,553. Density rose from about 801.7 people per square mile in 2010 to 857.7 in 2020, a far lower density than Garfield Heights or Gahanna.

In 2020 the Census found 11,195 households. Married couples headed 53.8 percent, children under 18 lived in 29.7 percent, and 26.7 percent were one-person households, including 12.6 percent where that person was 65 or older.

Green sits at about 1,198 feet of elevation within the Akron metropolitan area. A listing should name the city and the school district, Green Local Schools, since many Green addresses carry Akron-area ZIP codes.

sections.h2: What are the zoning and code rules in Green?
sections.html:
The city's Zoning Division issues permits, inspects new structures and enforces the City Code, and it also takes right-of-way applications for aprons and road openings. Its Zoning page lists the most common code complaints:

  • High grass
  • Litter, garbage and debris
  • Junk or inoperable vehicles
  • Storage of RVs, campers and boats
  • Property disrepair

Clear any of these before listing. The division is at the Central Administration Building, 1755 Town Park Blvd., and its phone is 330-896-6605. The Land Development Code is in Part Twelve of the city's codified ordinances.

The city page also names the Summit County Department of Building Standards in Akron and Summit County Public Health on West Market Street as permit and inspection agencies.

sections.h2: What does the Summit County Fiscal Office charge to transfer a Green deed?
sections.html:
Summit County's fee page sets the conveyance fee at $4.00 per $1,000 of price, rounded up to the next $100, and adds 50 cents for each lot in the legal description, even on exempt transfers. Hancock and Franklin counties show $3 per $1,000.

On the Property Transfer page, the department takes the DTE 100 statement of value or the DTE 100(EX) exemption form, under ORC 319.202 and 319.54(G)(3). Properly prepared forms must reach the Property Transfer Department by 3:30 p.m. to have the legal description approved the same business day. Under ORC 319.202 the value on the statement is the full consideration, mortgage or lien balances included, the grantor pays the fee, and willfully falsifying the value is prohibited.

The Recording Division is at 175 South Main Street, 4th floor, Akron. An unrecorded deed loses to a later buyer who had no notice of it, which is why ORC 5301.25 sends every deed to the county recorder. The same section adds a drafting rule: when a survey was made of the land being conveyed, the surveyor's name has to appear in the deed, and the county auditor can insist on it. Ask the Recording Division for the current per-page recording charge.

sections.h2: Which employers and amenities draw buyers to Green?
sections.html:
Wikipedia quotes the city's 2022 annual financial report: Green Local School District leads with 632 jobs, then

  • Summa Health System, 555
  • Fannie May Confection, 550
  • FedEx Custom Critical, 495
  • Diebold Nixdorf, 427
  • Target, 369

Interstate 77 serves the city, and the Akron-Canton Regional Airport lies partly inside Green and partly in Jackson Township. Green opened the first two-lane roundabout in Summit County in 2009 and had 11 roundabouts as of 2024.

Boettler Park, a 26-acre park with trails, fishing, picnicking and biking, and the Singer Lake Bog nature preserve are public spaces in the city. Public school students attend Green Local Schools. A mayor and a seven-member council run the city, with four of the council members chosen by ward and everyone limited to two consecutive four-year terms.

sections.h2: What should a Green seller know about pipelines and local history?
sections.html:
Green fought the NEXUS Pipeline in court starting in 2016 because the line runs near residential neighborhoods, wetlands and the Comet Lake Dam. Construction began in 2018 after the city reached a $7.5 million settlement. If your lot is near the route, check your title paperwork for any easement before a buyer asks.

From about 1950 farmers began selling land to developers, so Green houses range from older farm properties to newer subdivision homes.

sections.h2: Which sale routes work for a Green house on a deadline?
sections.html:
• Agent listing: a fit for move-in-ready homes where recent nearby sales give a clear price.
  • Investor sale: suited to dated houses, open code complaints, or an estate sale on a deadline.
  • Owner sale: saves commission but requires you to prepare the DTE 100 and deed paperwork.
  • Sale to a relative or neighbor: the exemption form may apply, and the 50 cent lot fee is owed either way.

Whichever route you pick, price the house against nearby Green sales, check for open zoning complaints, and pull together the survey and title papers. If the lot has a septic system, ask Summit County Public Health what records it keeps.

faqs.q: Who issues permits for a house in Green?
faqs.a: The city's Zoning Division handles zoning permits and inspections of new structures, and the Summit County Department of Building Standards is listed as the county agency.

faqs.q: How much is the Summit County conveyance fee on a Green sale?
faqs.a: The county's fee page shows $4.00 per $1,000, with the price rounded up to the next $100, plus 50 cents per lot. Forms in by 3:30 p.m. get same-day legal description approval.

faqs.q: Where does a Green deed get recorded?
faqs.a: In Akron, at the Fiscal Office Recording Division on South Main Street, because Ohio records a deed in the county where the land sits.
Green Local School District leads with 632 jobs in the city's 2022 financial report, ahead of Summa Health System, Fannie May Confection and FedEx Custom Critical.

faqs.q: How do I find out about code complaints on my Green house?
faqs.a: Call the Zoning Division at 330-896-6605. Overgrown grass, junk vehicles, stored RVs and general disrepair top its list of violations.
